newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lockheed sees Airbus cooperation on plane.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed sees Airbus cooperation on plane.

text.p: A Lockheed Martin executive said on Thursday he could envisage cooperation between his company and the Airbus Industrie consortium on building a new transport plane.

"I do see downstream the need for...a new world airlifter. I think there could be some partnerships with regards to particularly Lockheed Martin and Airbus," vice president for marketing Michael Smith told a business conference.
He said the new plane would meet "additional requirements beyond those for the FLA (Future Large Aircraft)," which is planned for tactical airlift for eight European armies.
Smith he did not see Lockheed Martin getting involved with the FLA work. The U.S. firm competes with its C130J Hercules product of which it has sold 25 units to Britain.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
